speaker: richard_quiney
text: You walked from London!

speaker: richard_quiney
text: Then you'll walk as far as my shop.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: It is not for myself, Will, it is for the town.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Master Quiney. My feet have had their hundred miles, and I am looked for at dinner.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: The meat will not wait on a shop.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: The town will keep a day. It will not keep a month. We have the whole north end in ashes, twice in fourteen months.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have heard you. I have not said yes.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: Half past six on Tuesday, then, at your father's board. Master Sturley comes with me. If the shop is too far for a pair of feet, the house is not.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Half past six on Tuesday, Master Quiney. The table knows of it. The shop does not.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: The wind came out of the south-west at two in the afternoon. The wind was not asking whose kiln had a fire under it.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: True, Mistress Shakespeare. And I sat in the Corporation pew and took the sermon on the neck for the borough.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Every malt-kiln in the parish had its eyes on the pavement before he was halfway through the text.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Twice in fourteen months was the first head. Strong drink was the second. The Sabbath was the third.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: She keeps the heads better than the parish clerk. She may keep them. I am not walking to the shop on the strength of them.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Judith had his voice before we were over the threshold. She will spend it at dinner if she is let.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Judith will keep her voice behind her teeth until we are out of the lane.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: The street is clear down Old Town. The children are ahead.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Let the boy's hand go, Richard Quiney. He has walked far enough this week.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: Done. Until Tuesday, at the house. My shop is by the Cross when a boot will bear you, and not before you say so.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Come to the house if you must. I have not promised the shop.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Nine of us down Old Town and nine of us back.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Walk on. Dinner is waiting, and the shop is still unpromised.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am behind you. At a walk.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: Not for myself. For the town. Tuesday will do to begin it.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: The three heads will keep till Tuesday. They do not need the shop to stay true.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: Then let the string go home. The porch is empty enough.
